rows.description: Someone asks for money or a lift, and you hesitate because of scams. Caution is legitimate. Offer safe help such as calling authorities or buying food, and trust your instincts without becoming hard-hearted.
A stranger helps you at a breakdown or in an emergency. Thank them warmly, get contact if appropriate, and pass the kindness on. Such moments remind us that society runs on quiet decency.
Helps within safe limits, checks the story where possible and does not give in to manipulation or guilt.
I fear being replaced and start clinging, checking who she sits with. Wise: tell her plainly I feel left out and ask for one plan just us. Clinging and testing her loyalty makes her feel trapped.

I see that friends can have other friends, and being happy for her costs me little. I say hi to the new girl and suggest a game for three. This maturity shows up as generosity, not as pretending I feel nothing.

Another girl whispers that my best friend now finds me boring, hoping to split us. Wise: check directly with my friend rather than trust the whisperer. Believing everything I hear lets others steer my friendships.
I like the new friend but feel like a traitor to my old one. I can hold both friendships, tell my old friend she still matters, and not hide things. Lying about where I was makes it worse.
The older toddler hits, whines or asks to be carried, wanting to know if there is still room for him. Wise parents reserve a little daily special time and let him help in small ways.
The older child regresses: wants a bottle, wets again, clings. It is a bid to be held like the baby. Meet it gently and briefly without mockery; it passes when he feels secure.
Hearing you are still my big boy while being cuddled tells the child love has not been used up. Words plus a lap, not just praise for being a good helper, keep him secure.

My parents openly favour a sibling in gifts, praise, or the will and I feel unseen and hurt. I say it calmly to them if safe, do not turn it into war with my sibling, and build my worth outside their approval.

I feel protective of my younger sibling as they start their life and I want to steer them. I offer support and listen, and I accept that their choices are theirs; controlling them out of love is still control.

I feel I was always compared with my brother or sister and now we compete over family property or attention. I remember the bond behind the contest; the wise move is to speak fairly and openly, not to keep score for decades.

After our parent's death, my sibling and I grieve differently and misread each other as cold or dramatic. I ask how they are coping, share memories together, and settle assets only after the first wave of grief has passed.
I think my sibling is stupid or lazy and say it so. Wise: notice contempt shuts down closeness and ask what I envy or fear. Harmful: cruelty in front of others.
My younger sibling follows me everywhere and copies me, and I am annoyed and secretly flattered. Wise: give some time and boundaries, remembering I am their model. Harmful: mocking their need.
I fight with my younger sibling yet turn fierce when outsiders tease them. Wise: this loyalty is real; show it more kindly at home too. Harmful: bossing them and calling it protection.

We fight over the phone, room, and parental attention, each keeping score. Wise: agree on clear shared rules and ask a parent to referee once. Immature: tattling, hiding things, and escalating each round.

You choose one person and its meaning goes beyond feelings. Wise: love shows in reliability, honest talk and making room for their growth. Immature: treating commitment as ownership or a performance for social media.
You notice what they do quietly, like showing up in a hard week. Wise: say thanks specifically and reciprocate. Immature: keeping a score of favours and sulking when they are not repaid.

rows.subtype: Partner × Pressure to define the relationship [Receiver]
rows.description: They ask where this is going and you feel cornered. Wise: be honest about what you know and do not know, and avoid stringing them along. Immature: dodging, or saying yes to avoid a scene.

You choose to believe them without proof at every moment. Wise: trust builds through small kept promises and is not blind; you can still notice red flags. Immature: testing them constantly to feel safe.
